correctness.rationale: The midpoint target bounds each coordinate difference by D/2 on a full-measure product box; the bilateral weight sum 3 proves failure at and above 3D/2 in the iid case, including the Dirac case. For each fixed arbitrary target separately, choose the farther support endpoint in each coordinate. Both endpoint neighborhoods have positive marginal mass, so disjoint translates of a fixed finite block have independent chances bounded below to contribute more than any r<3D/2. This proves nullity by Borel–Cantelli without an uncountable union over targets. De Finetti then integrates null masses below (3/2) ess inf D. Above it, slack permits covering the midpoints of a positive-measure sublevel of D by finitely many neighborhoods; one common constant target captures positive mass from the corresponding components. In the explicit mixture the weights sum to one, the positive Lebesgue-product part gives full support, and all components are atomless and mixing, with positive radii tending to zero. A mixture boundary assertion is not needed for the supremum: at d_*>0 an atomic midpoint among D=d_* components gives failure, whereas if that restricted midpoint law has no atoms then any fixed target can have positive critical-window mass for at most one midpoint: infinitely many coordinates separated from a component midpoint would provide infinitely many disjoint blocks with an extra positive center discrepancy and force escape by the same endpoint argument. This confirms that the frozen statement did not silently assume a boundary convention for mixtures. The frozen finite arithmetic checker was inspected, not run; neither it nor its recorded examples substitutes for the proof.
